chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Yaqub ibn Shu'ayb, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'If a wall contains different fruits, and some of them have ripened, there is no problem with selling them all together.'

key_terms.حَائِط: Wall (often used in fiqh to denote a source of produce like a tree or vineyard)

ai.seo_question: Can I sell all the fruits from a tree or wall if only some have ripened?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* clarifies the permissibility of selling mixed fruits from a single source when only a portion has ripened, resolving potential ambiguities in *gharar* (uncertainty) by establishing that partial maturity validates the entire transaction. It reflects the Shia juristic principle that the presence of a dominant, identifiable commodity allows for the sale of the whole, provided the specific items sold are distinguishable. This ruling is foundational in commercial jurisprudence (*Fiqh al-Mu'amalat*) for ensuring market fluidity while maintaining contractual validity.
